name: SQL Formatter for kiros33
summary: SQL formatter following the ansi-sql-format skill — tab-aligned AS/operators · WHERE 1=1 · dash lines around set operators (WASM · formatter extension)
description:
A SQL formatter extension (ABI v1.1 nx_ext_format). It reuses the app's Basic formatter core (nsql-format: lexer · layout · common options) and adds the kiros33 skill rules on top: vertical tab alignment of AS / comparison operators / ORDER BY direction (longest item → next tab stop · outliers get one tab on each side), AND/OR at the WHERE column, dash comment lines around UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / MINUS, WHERE 1=1 seed.
Common options (indent, comma position and gap, keyword case, one-line/multi-line lists, AND/OR position …) come from Preferences ▸ Editor ▸ SQL Formatting; ext.sqlfmt_kiros33.strict (default on) forces the skill values (tab · width 4 · leading comma · ",	" · 1=1 · UPPER · AND at line start · ";" on its own line). Extension-only rules live under Preferences ▸ Extensions ▸ SQL Formatter for kiros33. Use it once from the palette (Format With…), set it as the default formatter (Shift+Alt+F), or open Format Preview.
1.1.0: built on the Basic extension API (prepare → tweak → render), so every Basic option applies here too — automatic table aliases, table description comments, dialect translation, parenthesized AND/OR group seeds, gaps after AND/OR and around operators (4+ character operators get one space). PL/SQL block layout stays as written.
1.2.0: column aliases always get AS (ext.sqlfmt_kiros33.force_as, default on); items longer than the alignment outlier limit are left out of the tab alignment.
1.3.0: duplicate column names from joins get numbered / table-qualified / kept aliases (dup_alias); long window OVER (…) clauses break into PARTITION BY / ORDER BY / frame lines (window_break); the outlier limit (default 40) is measured from the first non-blank character and outliers get exactly one tab before and after AS / the operator; BETWEEN and IS [NOT] NULL are aligned as operators; ORDER BY direction alignment also covers items without a direction; the preview marks (▶ preview line n) for every extension setting now come from the extension itself.
1.3.1: multi-line items (a window OVER (…) closing on its own line) join the AS alignment block, so the ")" line gets the same AS column as its neighbours.
1.3.2: rebuilt on the updated Basic core — EXEC statements (EXEC + SELECT … INTO formatted as a block, EXEC + procedure/package call on one line), script command lines end at the line, PL/SQL blocks pass through only to their END/"/"/GO (statements after a block are formatted), ${name:format} / N'…' / q'[…]' kept as single tokens, unary signs and ::casts stay glued.
1.3.3: with keyword case = keep, an alias AS keeps its original spelling (as / As) and still joins the AS alignment.
